title: Arc: Tidy Tabs
how: ffmpeg streamed the video from its URL into cutscene's measure (256 px luma, every frame); nothing saved but these numbers and stills in scratch
whyTopTier: One sentence is split across cards ('Don't worry' … 'Tab' … 'Tidy Tabs') with the proof between them, and the UI is cropped to the one component that changes, the sidebar, at about ×2.5. 20.5 s.
instrument: The camera barely moves; what moves is a crop. The one pull (×0.45 at 6.25 s) reveals the page beside the sidebar.

byEye.zoom: the sidebar alone fills half the frame (about ×2.5 its size in a full window); one pull-back to sidebar plus page
byEye.cards: 5, bold white on Arc blue: 'Don't worry', 'Tab', 'Tidy Tabs', 'Now available in Arc', 'arc.net'; plus the logo; each 1.1–1.8 s
byEye.cursor: native macOS pointer at the enlarged scale
byEye.frame: the sidebar crop sits on a full-bleed photo (forest, clouds, salmon), the user's Arc theme
byEye.sound: an audio track with rhythmic onsets (not listened to)

curveFits.best: AE easy ease on linear scale, 1505 ms (2.21%)
curveFits.others: spring ζ=0.8 on linear scale, ω 3/s, 1250 ms (4.63%)

classify: Hand-edited feature reel of real UI, cropped to a component and set on photo backdrops (Arc's themes). Conventions: brand-colour cards, cut-not-move, a URL end card.

diagnose.observation: Only the sidebar is on screen when it's the subject.
diagnose.principle: Crop to the component: the frame holds exactly the element that changes, so nothing competes for attention.

diagnose.observation: The sentence 'Don't worry … Tab … Tidy Tabs' is interrupted by its own evidence.
diagnose.principle: Call and response: claim, proof, claim, proof keeps the viewer reading the UI as the answer to the card.

diagnose.observation: Each theme change happens at a cut.
diagnose.principle: Continuity by component: the sidebar keeps its position across the cut while the backdrop changes, so the cut reads as the same object in a new context (a match cut on position).

teaches.text: Crop to the component: frame one element's box at large scale instead of pushing into the whole window.
Hand-edited reels reframe by cutting, not by moving.
A sentence split across cards, interleaved with UI.

critique.like: Every UI shot answers the card before it; nothing is shown that the copy didn't promise.
critique.wish: The crop hides the page, so it's never clear which tab the user is on when the sidebar tidies.
critique.wonder: Would a match cut on the sidebar (same box, new theme) work as cutscene's transition between two scenes of one app?
